arxiv-1803-05204.title: Some remarks on Yamabe solitons
arxiv-1803-05204.creator: Debabrata Chakraborty, Yadab Chandra Mandal and Shyamal Kumar Hui ∗
arxiv-1803-05204.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Debabrata Chakraborty, Yadab Chandra Mandal and Shyamal Kumar Hui ∗. In this paper we have obtained evolution of some geometric quantities on a compact Riemannian manifold M n M^{n} when the metric is a Yamabe soliton. Using these quantities we have obtained bound on the soliton constant. We have proved that the commutator of two soliton vector fields with the same metric in a given conformal class produces a Killing vector field.

arxiv-2111-08192.title: SALSA-Lite: A Fast and Effective Feature for Polyphonic Sound Event Localization and Detection with Microphone Arrays
arxiv-2111-08192.creator: Thi Ngoc Tho Nguyen, Douglas L. Jones, Karn N. Watcharasupat, Huy Phan, Woon-Seng Gan
arxiv-2111-08192.description: Abstract Polyphonic sound event localization and detection (SELD) has many practical applications in acoustic sensing and monitoring. However, the development of real-time SELD has been limited by the demanding computational requirement of most recent SELD systems. In this work, we introduce SALSA-Lite, a fast and effective feature for polyphonic SELD using microphone array inputs.

arxiv-2301-12994.title: Transverse structure of the pion beyond leading twist with basis light-front quantization
arxiv-2301-12994.creator: Zhimin Zhu, Zhi Hu, Jiangshan Lan, Chandan Mondal, Xingbo Zhao, James P. Vary, (BLFQ Collaboration)
arxiv-2301-12994.description: Abstract We investigate the twist- 3 3 transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution functions (TMDs) of the pion with basis light-front quantization. The twist-3 TMDs are not independent and can be decomposed into twist- 2 2 and genuine twist- 3 3 terms from the equations of motion (EOM).

arxiv-2411-01925.description: Abstract . Objects, in the real world, rarely occur in isolation and exhibit typical arrangements governed by their independent utility, and their expected interaction with humans and other objects in the context. For example, a chair is expected near a table, and a computer is expected on top.

arxiv-2503-06249.title: Higgs production from anomalous gluon dynamics
arxiv-2503-06249.creator: Ulrich Haisch
arxiv-2503-06249.description: Abstract We present a two-loop analysis of the contributions to Higgs production via gluon-gluon fusion arising from the triple-gluon operator in the Standard Model effective field theory (SMEFT). Our discussion covers all aspects of renormalization group (RG) improved perturbation theory, including matching and running within the SMEFT.

arxiv-2504-13213.title: A Model of Realistic Flavor Symmetry: Origin of Fermion Mass, Flavor Mixing and Leptogenesis
arxiv-2504-13213.creator: Wei-Min Yang
arxiv-2504-13213.description: Abstract Abstract : I proposed a unified model of particle physic and cosmology in [ 1 ] , which can simultaneously account for these origin of the inflation, dark energy, dark matter, neutrino mass and baryon asymmetry. I here focus on the fermion flavor issues in the unified model, which were not addressed previously.

arxiv-2509-26065.title: Runtime Energy Monitoring for RISC-V Soft-Cores
arxiv-2509-26065.creator: Alberto Scionti and Paolo Savio and Francesco Lubrano and Olivier Terzo and Marco Ferretti and Florin Apopei and Juri Bellucci and Ennio Spano and Luca Carriere
arxiv-2509-26065.description: Abstract Energy efficiency is one of the major concern in designing advanced computing infrastructures. From single nodes to large-scale systems (data centers), monitoring the energy consumption of the computing system when applications run is a critical task. Designers and application developers often rely on software tools and detailed architectural models to extract meaningful information and determine the system energy consumption.

pmc-10535075.title: Study of the Removal Efficiency of Chromium Ions Using a Membrane by Electro-Kinetic Technique from Sludge
pmc-10535075.creator: Nabaa S. Hadi, Huda H. Awadh
pmc-10535075.description: Recently, electro-kinetic (EK) remediation has become more popular as a novel method for removing chromium contamination from soil. This approach, however, is ineffective since it uses both cationic and anionic forms of chromium. In this study, a membrane-based technique was employed to increase the efficiency of the electro-kinetic removal of chromium.

pmc-10738162.title: ANALYSIS OF CONVERSATIONAL ENTRAINMENT AMONG OLDER PERSONS WITH ADRD AND UNIMPAIRED ADULTS
pmc-10738162.creator: Christine Williams, Joseph McKinley, Charles Cooper, Nurgun Erdol, Christopher Beetle
pmc-10738162.description: Social isolation threatens the health of older adults, particularly those with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD). Our research uses measures of behavioral coordination to quantify the entrainment of an individual’s behavior to the collective dynamics of a group to which they belong, aiming to identify useful strategies to reduce social isolation for persons with ADRD in therapeutic group contexts.

pmc-11447111.title: Predicting multiple sclerosis disease progression and outcomes with machine learning and MRI-based biomarkers: a review
pmc-11447111.creator: Hibba Yousef, Brigitta Malagurski Tortei, Filippo Castiglione
pmc-11447111.description: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a demyelinating neurological disorder with a highly heterogeneous clinical presentation and course of progression. Disease-modifying therapies are the only available treatment, as there is no known cure for the disease. Careful selection of suitable therapies is necessary, as they can be accompanied by serious risks and adverse effects such as infection.

pmc-11558105.title: Wolbachia in Antarctic terrestrial invertebrates: Absent or undiscovered?
pmc-11558105.creator: Svitlana Serga, Pavlo A. Kovalenko, Oleksandr M. Maistrenko, Gwenaëlle Deconninck, Oleksandra Shevchenko, Nataliia Iakovenko, Yurii Protsenko, Andrij Susulovsky, Łukasz Kaczmarek, Mariia Pavlovska, Peter Convey, Iryna Kozeretska
pmc-11558105.description: Interactions between a host organism and its associated microbiota, including symbiotic bacteria, play a crucial role in host adaptation to changing environmental conditions. Antarctica provides a unique environment for the establishment and maintenance of symbiotic relationships. One of the most extensively studied symbiotic bacteria in invertebrates is Wolbachia pipientis, which is associated with a wide variety of invertebrates.

pmc-11595731.title: The Sternocleidomastoid Muscle Reverse Pad: A “Safety Net” in Catastrophic Tracheal Surgery Situation
pmc-11595731.creator: Sara Mantovani, Delia Giovanniello, Massimo O Jaus, Payaningal R Somanath
pmc-11595731.description: Background: This paper presents the outcomes of employing the inferiorly based rotated sternocleidomastoid muscle flap in complex tracheal reconstruction/repair scenarios, focusing on the key objectives of ensuring stable airway, functional digestive tract and patient survival. Methods: A retrospective analysis was performed for patients treated at two medical centers (A.O. San Camillo Forlanini, Rome, and A.O.U.

pmc-11736334.title: Serum progesterone measurement on the day of fresh embryo transfer and its correlation with pregnancy success rates: A prospective analysis
pmc-11736334.creator: Carla Maria Franco Dias, Suelen Maria Parizotto Furlan, Rui Alberto Ferriani, Paula Andrea de Albuquerque Salles Navarro
pmc-11736334.description: Highlights•Studies are inconclusive about the existence of a serum progesterone concentration correlated with higher clinical pregnancy rates in fresh embryo transfer after controlled ovarian stimulation cycles.•In fresh embryo transfer cycles, serum progesterone concentration may merely reflect factors associated with a favorable gestational prognosis rather than being a direct predictor of clinical pregnancy.

pmc-12447372.title: Alexithymia as a Bridge Between Negative Affect and Schizotypy: A Cross‐Sectional Network Model
pmc-12447372.creator: Ercan Ozdemir, Angus MacBeth, Helen Griffiths
pmc-12447372.description: BackgroundSchizotypy provides a theoretically grounded framework for investigating psychosis proneness, reflecting a multidimensional structure that parallels the positive, negative and disorganized symptoms of schizophrenia. Alexithymia, a trait characterized by difficulties in identifying (DIF) and describing feelings (DDF) and a tendency towards externally oriented thinking (EOT), has been robustly linked to schizophrenia.

pmc-13242145.title: Virtual gifting as affective monetization: a meta-analysis of behavioral antecedents in live game streaming platforms
pmc-13242145.creator: Siwat Chokpaisan, Charin Suwanwong, Jakkrit Thavorn
pmc-13242145.description: Virtual gifting is an important monetization mechanism in live game streaming, but prior evidence remains fragmented across psychological, social, and platform-oriented explanations. This study conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of empirical research published between 2015 and 2025 to synthesize construct-level antecedents associated with virtual gifting in live game streaming and closely related live streaming contexts.

pmc-13377616.title: Liver Injury Associated With Irregular Herbal Products: A Translational Case Series With Chemical Authentication and Causality Assessment Using the Updated RUCAM
pmc-13377616.creator: Ferdinando Lucas Góis, Rebeca Santos do Amaral de Souza, Raymundo Paraná, Vinícius Nunes, Genario Oliveira Santos Júnior, Ademir Evangelista do Vale
pmc-13377616.description: BackgroundHerb‐induced liver injury (HILI) represents an increasing diagnostic challenge owing to the widespread use of herbal and dietary supplements (HDS), which are frequently consumed without reliable information regarding their composition or safety. Mischaracterized products may obscure causal attributes and mimic primary herbal hepatotoxicity.
